Chapter 9: Facing the Present—Choices and Consequences
Right now, our world’s at a crossroads. We’re facing some pretty big challenges—climate change, shrinking resources, and a population that just keeps on growing. The choices you and I make today? They’re going to shape the world for generations to come.
Picture this: in the middle of a busy city, a group of friends sits together in a packed café. They chat about their jobs, their families, and their dreams for the future. But there’s an undercurrent—some worry about what they see in the news. Wildfires, floods, storms that seem to get worse every single year. Others try to tune it out and focus on the little joys—good coffee, laughter, just making it through the day. But the big questions linger. What kind of world will their children inherit? And what can they actually do to make things better?
When the problems feel so huge, it’s tempting to feel powerless. Maybe you’ve thought, “Someone else will figure this out. Maybe new technology, or government policy, or just plain luck will save the day.” But if you look back at history, it’s clear—waiting for someone else to step up is almost never enough. Real change? It begins with the small choices we make every single day. What we buy. How we live. What we truly value.
Here’s something to remember: every action matters, even if the impact isn’t obvious right away. The world is shaped by millions of tiny decisions, made by regular people just like you and me. The challenge is to make those choices with care—not just thinking about today, but about tomorrow too.
It’s easy to fall into the habit of thinking, “My actions don’t matter. The problems are too big.” But the truth is, change is possible—and it starts with each of us. The future isn’t set in stone. It’s going to be shaped by the choices we make right now, by our willingness to learn from what’s come before, and to imagine a better way forward.
So, as you head into the rest of your day, maybe ask yourself—what’s one small choice you can make, starting today, that could help build a better tomorrow?
